v.why: Without edge 4, removing the edge 0->3 path leaves almost no route to the output, so accuracy collapses (pairs 14/18/22 vs 13/17/21).
When edge 4 is absent, edge 5 is one of only two inputs to the output node, so deleting it hurts far more (79/80 vs 77/78).
With edge 5 missing, the output relies on node 1 via edge 4, so cutting edge 0 removes nearly all conv computation (84 vs 83).
Adding a residual input->output path where none existed gives a much larger gain than swapping out an existing op (41 vs 42-44).
Filling an empty input->output edge restores a shortcut path, which helps much more than replacing a conv there (74 vs 73).
Without the input->output skip, an identity edge into the output restores residual-like gradient flow in a deep all-conv cell (90 vs 89).
A skip into the output compensates for a missing input->output shortcut, so it helps far more when edge 3 is none (92 vs 91).
Edge 5 only carries useful signal if node 2 receives a strong input, which a conv on edge 1 provides (7 vs 8, 100 vs 99, 3 vs 2).
Replacing a parameter-free pooling op on the first edge with a conv adds a lot of learnable capacity feeding the rest of the cell (28, 31, 32).
When edge 0 is none, edge 1 is the only path into node 2 and the edge 5 path, so a conv there adds essential capacity (39, 40 vs parents with conv on edge 0).

Ten conditional hypotheses, each based on contrasts between matched parent pairs in the 100 experiments. Most of the patterns come down to connectivity. An edit matters most when it creates or removes the only remaining path, or the only identity path, from the input to the output.

1. **Edge 3 → none is worse when edge 4 = none.** Pairs 14/18/22 vs 13/17/21: −56/−54/−39 on CIFAR-10 vs −26/+18/+9.
2. **Edge 5 → none is worse when edge 4 = none.** Pairs 79/80 vs 77/78. Without edge 4, removing edge 5 leaves only edge 3 into the output.
3. **Edge 0 → none is worse when edge 5 = none.** Pair 84 vs 83: −28.4 vs −4.2 on CIFAR-10.
4. **Edge 3 → skip_connect is better when edge 3 = none.** Experiment 41 (+25.8/+34.4/+15.1) vs 42–44, which replace convs or pooling.
5. **Edge 3 → avg_pool_3x3 is better when edge 3 = none.** Pair 74 vs 73.
6. **Edge 5 → skip_connect is better when edge 3 = none.** Pair 90 vs 89.
7. **Edge 4 → skip_connect is better when edge 3 = none.** Pair 92 vs 91.
8. **Edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3 is better when edge 1 = nor_conv_3x3.** Pairs 7/8, 100/99, 3/2. Pair 1/4 is the one inconsistency: it gains more on CIFAR-100 but less on ImageNet16-120.
9. **Edge 0 → nor_conv_3x3 is better when edge 0 = avg_pool_3x3.** Experiments 28, 31, 32 show large gains on all three datasets except a −2.6 on ImageNet16-120 in 28.
10. **Edge 1 → nor_conv_3x3 is better when edge 0 = none.** Experiments 39 and 40 show large gains on all datasets, while the parents with edge 0 = nor_conv_3x3 give mixed results.
